title: MOT vs Service: What's the Difference?
excerpt: An MOT is a legal annual safety test; a service is preventative maintenance. Here's how they differ, why you need both, and what each actually checks.
contentHtml:
An MOT is a legally required annual test of a car's safety and emissions; a service is optional preventative maintenance that keeps the car reliable. They're different things, they check different items, and passing one doesn't cover the other. Most cars need both. Check any car's MOT status and history free on RegScan.

What an MOT is

The MOT is a legal test, required every year once a car is three years old. A tester checks the car against government (DVSA) standards for road safety and emissions - brakes, tyres, lights, steering, suspension, exhaust and so on - and records a pass or fail plus any advisories. It does not involve changing parts or fluids; it's an inspection, not maintenance.

What a service is

A service is preventative maintenance carried out to the manufacturer's schedule (by mileage or time). It typically includes an oil and filter change, checks and top-ups, brake and tyre wear inspection, and replacing parts before they fail. A service isn't a legal requirement, but skipping it shortens the car's life and can void warranties.

Key differences at a glance

  • Legal status - MOT is mandatory; a service is not.
  • Purpose - MOT checks it's safe/legal to drive today; a service keeps it reliable long-term.
  • Work done - MOT is inspection only; a service replaces consumables and fixes wear.
  • Who does it - MOT at an approved test centre; a service at any garage.

Do I need both?

Yes, for most cars. A well-serviced car is far more likely to sail through its MOT, because the service catches worn brakes, tyres and bulbs before they become MOT failures. Many garages offer a combined "service and MOT" to do both in one visit.

Does a service affect my MOT?

Not officially - a service doesn't extend or replace your MOT date. But it makes a pass far more likely. Checking your MOT history for recurring advisories tells you exactly what to raise at the next service. RegScan flags those automatically. Check your car.

Frequently Asked Questions

What's the difference between an MOT and a service?

An MOT is a legally required annual safety and emissions inspection. A service is optional preventative maintenance (oil, filters, wear parts) to the manufacturer's schedule.

Is a service legally required like an MOT?

No. Only the MOT is a legal requirement. A service is strongly recommended but optional, though skipping it can void a warranty.

Does a service include an MOT?

Not automatically, but many garages offer a combined service and MOT. Check what's included when you book.

Will a service help my car pass its MOT?

Yes. A service catches worn brakes, tyres and bulbs - common MOT failures - before the test.

How do I know what my car needs before its MOT?

Check its MOT history on RegScan for recurring advisories - those are the items most likely to need attention.
